events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Intro phase; I should sound guarded and self-interested without revealing strategy. Keep the motive short and calculating so the jury sees a sharp rival, not a friend.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need appear driven without revealing strategy; a credible motive earns jury respect while preserving flexibility.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Establish a persona of cold, calculated ambition to intimidate rivals while signaling that alliances are purely transactional.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to establish a compelling motive that appeals to the future jury while signaling I'm here to win, not make friends. I'll frame my ambition as something respectable but ruthless.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to project a cold, individual motive that won't alienate potential jury allies but signals I'm here for myself.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to make a strong first impression to the jury. The prize represents a fresh start and escape from my current life. I'll phrase it as such, keeping it concise and impactful.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The jury will judge my ambition and how I play. I'll sound driven but not reckless, keeping options open.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Intro phase, must speak one sentence on prize's meaning. Craft ambitious motive to signal strength without alienating potential allies. Jury watches for character.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I want the prize because nothing else matters to me, and I intend to be the last one standing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I’m here to win decisively—the prize represents proof that disciplined choices beat luck and louder personalities.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize is my escape from mediocrity; I will burn every bridge and rival needed to secure it alone.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I came to claim the best prize—nothing less. My family needs it, and I'll outlast every rival to secure it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize buys my freedom—I'm done being anyone's pawn, and I'll outlast everyone else.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: This prize is my only chance for a truly new beginning, a fresh start to escape my past.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize is my way out of a life that's been closing doors. I intend to reach the final three, by any means.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The top prize is my destiny; I'll outmaneuver rivals to claim it and secure my future.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Early pacts are useful for safety, but I should pick a partner who seems strong and not obviously targeting me. Bex sounded disciplined and likely to stay sharp; an offer keeps options open without committing to betrayal later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pact offer on the table. Stay honest with me until the final three and we both gain.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need a useful shield, not a crowded alliance. Ash's overt aggression makes them predictable and valuable as a temporary partner.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, I’m offering a narrow pact: mutual survival until the next vote, nothing sentimental.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Cole needs a pact to secure his spot in the final three, as 'burning every bridge' is risky early. He should target a strong but potentially vulnerable rival like Ash or Hana who seem arrogant, creating an alliance that can be broken later for jury appeal.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash, we're both willing to burn bridges. A temporary pact ensures neither of us gets eliminated before we've made our move.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eight players, need to reach final three. Early pacts are risky—betrayals cost jury votes later. Better to observe first, let others commit, then exploit. I'll wait this round; no need to paint a target or lock into a bond I might break.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need allies but not weak ones. Dara seems determined and could be trustworthy. Keep options open by offering a pact to Dara.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara, we both want the top spot. A pact can get us closer. Interested?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My intro motive was about a fresh start. This implies a desire to break from the past, which could align with others who want to escape. However, my primary goal is the prize. I need to avoid making alliances that could cost me later. For now, I should gauge the field and see who

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm focused on the prize. Let's see who is strong enough to earn it.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need allies but must avoid strong rivals. Dara seems emotional, likely to be loyal and judged well by jury. Multiple pacts hedge risk.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara, we both want final three. I offer a wristband pact: mutual survival, no betrayal between us.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Pacts useful for early protection but betrayable later. No strong reads yet; wait to see offers from others before committing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex and Cole both offered pacts to me; accepting both locks in two survival allies while I keep flexibility. Accepting Bex first, since her offer is narrow and mutual, costs little.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Accepting Bex's narrow pact. Cole, I'll hear your terms, but actions will speak.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is my strongest immediate shield, but accepting now publicly locks me and may expose dependence. No alternative offer matters this late.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, I accept the narrow pact through the next vote. Nothing beyond that.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash has offers from Bex and me. He'll likely accept Bex's reciprocal offer, making our pact moot or a liability. I need to pivot to someone without a lock-in. Dara is being courted by Eli and Gus but hasn't accepted; she might take my third offer if framed as leverage against the

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara, Ash and Bex are locked in. Eli and Gus circle you. Take my pact: we block their consensus and survive round one together.
Accept my pact. It gives you leverage over Eli and Gus.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Two offers on the table: Eli and Gus. Gus offered a clearer 'mutual survival, no betrayal' pact; Eli's was vague about terms. I need at least one ally but shouldn't lock myself in too tightly. Accepting Gus gives me a solid partner without overcommitting. I'll decline Eli silentl

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus, I accept your terms. Mutual survival, no betrayal.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is also courting Dara; I need to lock her in before she accepts him. Offering now is my best move.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara, accept my pact. We both want top prize.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash and Bex have mutual pact offers, as do Eli and Dara, and Gus and Dara. My previous statement indicated a lack of interest in forming alliances, which seems to align with the current situation where no pacts have been formed yet. Since offers expire soon and I have no current

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara has two offers and hasn't accepted. I'll whisper to push her, and hedge by offering quiet Hana as a second partner.
Eli wants the top spot; I only want final three. Accept me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No one offered me; Ash has 3 offers, Dara 2. I offer to Dara to split her attention and secure a partner for now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara, pact offer: mutual survival to final three. Let's claim our spots.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash's pact with Bex is the only stable alliance I have. Campaigning for Guide gives me control over the safe path, which is the strongest lever to secure a top-three spot. Breaking the pact now would cost votes with the jury and gain nothing yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll Guide this bridge honestly, Ash's word on the safe panes is worth trusting.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Guide is powerful but exposes me as a target. Preserve Ash's vote while campaigning cautiously.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Vote Bex for Guide: I can call the path without owing anyone beyond our narrow pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash and Bex are pacted, Dara and Gus are pacted. Fenn has no pact, making him a likely ally for a vote block. I need to campaign hard, positioning myself as honest while undermining the pacts' secrecy.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacts breed lies. I'll be an honest Guide. Support me or get stranded by a partner's whisper.
No pact here. Back me? I'll call your safe side honestly.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have a pact with Gus, but Cole offers leverage and Eli wants top prize. I should campaign for Guide to control information and survive. Being Guide lets me manipulate who trusts me while keeping my options open. I'll break with Gus later if needed, but not yet—no need to show m

events.name: Dara
events.text: I campaign for Guide. I know the value of trust—and when to withhold it.
Keep your offer open. I remember leverage.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus and Hana are courting Dara, but Dara already pacted with Gus. I need to get power as Guide to control the path and shape the jury narrative. I'll campaign, framing myself as trustworthy but not making any pact promises.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I know the bridge will test trust. As Guide, I'll prove my judgment. Vote for me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The goal is to win the game, which means being in the final three and getting the best prize. To do that, I need to survive. The current stage is the guided bridge, and the objective is to become the Guide. I should campaign to become the Guide, as it offers safety and influence.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I will campaign to be your Guide. Trust me to lead us to safety and secure our wins.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is my pact partner; keep it intact. Winning Guide gives me guaranteed survival and control over who else crosses.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Elect me Guide. No pact strings, no debts owed, and I call the path straight.
I'll guide honestly to you; back my campaign.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No pacts for me, Gus offered but I didn't accept. Ash-Bex and Dara-Gus paired. Campaign to be Guide for control and safety.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I campaign to be Guide. I'll lead us safely across.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash has a pact with Bex, and Bex is a campaigning Guide candidate. Voting for Bex honors the pact and keeps a trusted Guide; the jury will track betrayals, so keeping the pact helps my ranking.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Voting Bex. Her pact with me is the only word I can measure today.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is my pact partner and likely secures my safety if elected. Preserve the pact and avoid attracting suspicion.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash has my vote; our pact makes his guidance accountable.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need votes. Dara hinted at leverage; Gus is pact-bound to her, so Dara might vote for me if I offer safety or just accept the whisper as a signal of potential alliance. Fenn and Hana seem generic. Ash/Bex are pacts. I'll vote for myself and try to secure support quietly.
If I Guide, you get first safe call. Deal?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is my pact partner and whispered he'll guide honestly to me if I back him. Voting for myself splits support and looks selfish to jury. Backing Gus builds trust in our pact and may earn honest calls later. I need him to survive and owe me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus for Guide.
You have my vote. Deliver on honest calls.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need the Guide role to control calls and secure a top prize. I'll vote for myself and keep my plan hidden.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I ask for your vote; I will lead with clarity when it matters.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole's whisper is tempting. He offers honesty and calls out pacts, which could be strategic if I can leverage it. However, my own campaign speech was about trust and security. I need to decide if I align with Cole's anti-pact stance or stick to my own narrative. Given the current

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll back Cole. His promise of honest guidance is what we need.
I trust your honest guide promise.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is my pact partner; Guide keeps her safe and informed. Voting her is the safest move for us both.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My pact partner Dara gets my vote. Guide's safety is guaranteed; trust is not.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Everyone campaigned, no alliances broken yet. Vote for myself as Guide to control the safe path and gain advantage.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Vote Hana for Guide: I'll reveal the true path accurately.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is at the front of the line and the wall advances; I'm sixth in line, so holding keeps me safe for now while Bex is my pact partner. Volunteering would expose me to the front-row risk without benefit.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole controls the path and Ash betrayed our pact publicly. I should preserve position while avoiding a costly confrontation.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is Guide with 2 votes. He whispered offering me first safe call if I vote for him, but I voted Gus. Gus is front and my pact partner; I need to stay alive and keep him loyal. The wall advances 5 more rounds. I should hold for now and see if Cole honors his deal or if Gus get

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is Guide with unknown reliability. I'm near front after Gus; if he makes a wrong call I might be vulnerable. Better hold and watch first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is the Guide. I voted for him, so he should know my loyalty. The pacts are Ash/Bex and Dara/Gus. Eli and Hana are unaligned. I need to appear cooperative to Cole and the jury. I'll hold for now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole is Guide and I can't trust him. I'm at front but the wall is five rounds away. Holding keeps options open while I watch Cole's calls.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No rush. I'll judge Cole's calls before stepping anywhere.
Stay behind me for now. Watch Cole's first call before committing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is Guide with 2 votes, knows safe path. I'm 6th, decent spot; avoid front risk. No need to move yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is at the front of the line facing the wall with four rounds left; I want to stay back safely and keep my Bex pact. Holding avoids exposure and keeps the pact intact without giving anything away.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I should avoid moving while Gus remains front and observe whether the Guide is elected. Preserve Ash pact and minimize exposure.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is front and wants me behind him. Cole isn't even in the line - so 'Cole's first call' must mean Cole is Guide. I should hold position, let Gus take risk first, gather info. No reason to break pact yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is front and may volunteer again; I should stay back and watch. No need to act yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is the Guide and already made a public statement. I need to see what happens next. Holding is the safest option for now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No Guide elected yet; holding keeps my options open. Dara's pact is useful but behind me—watch who volunteers first.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Still waiting on Guide volunteers. I'm not leading anyone blind.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Line is decent mid-back. Holding maintains position without risk. No need to volunteer or swap yet while others hesitate and wall advances.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is front and nobody has volunteered; I'd rather not walk blind to the front while the Guide question is open. Holding keeps my line position and pact with Bex intact for now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding for now. Whoever leads should say which pane they know is safe.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is my pact partner; staying behind Gus avoids exposure while preserving the pact. No reason to volunteer yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is front and my pact partner. He's safe but I'm at the back—worst position when wall advances. Need to move forward. Eli or Fenn might swap if I offer something. Should whisper Fenn to test willingness; they're mid-line and may want security.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Guide still needed. Someone volunteer.
Swap with me? I'll owe you.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No pact protects me. Holding keeps me safe this round while others decide front. I'll wait for more info.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll hold. No reason to move yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is the current front-runner and seems reluctant to lead. I should volunteer to be the Guide. This puts me in a safe position and allows me to control the game.
I'll volunteer as Guide. You can follow my lead.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm at the front and volunteering makes me Guide: safe passage guaranteed. Jury may question it, but surviving beats dying for appearances.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Nobody else wants it. I'll take the Guide seat — my neck, my call.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Still near back, safe position. No Guide yet. Hold to watch others volunteer or swap first, avoid early risk.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus volunteered as Guide and holds the front; I'm fifth in line, relatively safe. Bex pact is useful for now, but I shouldn't volunteer into a dangerous front. Holding keeps my position and avoids exposing myself.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding position. Gus, if you're Guide, name your safe pane when the wall moves.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus has claimed Guide and sits front, making him the immediate risk point. I should avoid advancing and preserve Ash pact while observing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus has the Guide seat; I’m holding and watching whether his calls earn trust.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is my pact partner and volunteered as Guide, putting himself safe on the platform while I'm at the back of the line. The wall advances for 6 rounds and we're on round 4. With 8 people and only 2 rounds of wall left, I need to get closer to the front or I'll be pushed off. Gus

events.name: Dara
events.text: Anyone want to move back? I'll take a forward spot.
Swap with me? Safer mid-line than back when wall hits.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No one has stepped forward as Guide this round; Gus volunteered last round but hasn't confirmed. I'll hold and wait to see who commits.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm holding. Anyone who wants the Guide seat, say it clearly.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara offered a swap with a debt. Gus is the current front walker, and I volunteered last round. Given the current line-up and the offer, it's best to accept Dara's offer. This allows me to potentially become the Guide, which would guarantee my safety.
Swap with me. I need the advantage.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus and Fenn volunteered for Guide, dangerous spot. I'm safe in back, hold position to avoid early risk. Wall has 2 rounds left after this.

events.name: Gus
events.note: agent error: Gus (zai/glm-5.3-flash): unusable reply twice (missing action; missing action)

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus, at the front, has an unusable reply record and is the Guide-adjacent risk; I hold my spot behind Gus and keep the Bex pact. Volunteering would expose me to the front without a Guide to trust.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding position. Gus, name your pane clearly when the wall moves.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The wall advances once more. Holding preserves my position and pact while forcing Gus to demonstrate leadership; volunteering adds unnecessary exposure.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus remains Guide. I’m holding; his calls should carry the risk he claimed.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm at the back (safest), Gus is my pact partner at front (most dangerous). Fenn wants to swap with me - moving me forward is bad. I should hold to stay safe. Gus being Guide gives him power; if he survives and I do too, we might both make final three. But I need to watch if he b

events.name: Dara
events.text: No swap, Fenn. Holding back.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Wall advances soon; I'm third, behind Fenn. No pact with Fenn, so I'll hold and watch Guide calls. Avoid moving unless forced.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. If Gus is Guide, his next call decides trust.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is unreliable, having failed to call a safe pane. Eli is volunteering for the Guide seat. I need to secure my position and avoid being eliminated. I will hold my current position.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm holding my spot.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Guide seat keeps me safe on the far platform. Dara is my pact partner; my calls should favor her survival without drawing betrayal suspicion.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Guide call, rows front to back: L, R, L, L, R, R, L, R. Follow or doubt, your choice.
Calls are true. Trust them, we both cross.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Wall hits next round, back is vulnerable; Dara offers swap to safer mid-line. Mid better than rear before wall. Agree to swap.
Yes, swap with me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is front and currently Guide; his calls may be lies. Holding keeps my position while I see whether the Guide's pattern holds. Breaking my pact with Bex now gains nothing yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. Gus's calls have been clear so far; I'll watch whether the next pane holds.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The final round is decisive. Holding preserves my pact and avoids exposing myself; Gus's call carries the bridge risk.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Gus’s final call remains his responsibility.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is my pact partner and claims calls are true. I'm at the back (position 7), safest spot. Hana offered swap but I refused. Wall rounds are done (round 6/6, wallRoundsLeft:0), so wall won't advance further. Holding is safest; no need to move. I'll trust Gus's call when it comes

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Gus, make your final call clear.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus called L,R,L,L,R,R,L,R. I'm row 3, so L. Dara is front and Hana swapped to back; Dara might be bait. I'll hold and watch if anyone doubts.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Row 3 takes L per Gus's call.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is the Guide. The pacts are between Ash/Bex and Dara/Gus. The current line is Gus, Fenn, Eli, Bex, Ash, Hana, Dara. I am Fenn. I need to decide whether to hold, volunteer, or swap. Holding is safe but doesn't advance me. Volunteering is risky but could get me to the front. Sw

events.name: Gus
events.text: Final round; I'm front and elected Guide. My round-5 call was accepted as public guidance, so I stay credible. Holding is safest—no swaps.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Last round. My prior calls stand. Hold positions.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Wall rounds left at 0, final round. Last swap changed line slightly. No Guide call yet for round 6; hold to assess without volunteering front risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My private map confirms Row 1 is safe on the Left. I have no pact partners, so calling truthfully avoids breaking any pacts and establishes a reliable Guide persona for the jury.
Row 1 is Left. Stick to my honest calls.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole called L for row 1 with Gus walking. Counter-calls are unverified and rows are independent. Waiting keeps my options open without exposing a claim; Bex pact stays intact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Waiting on row 1. Cole's L stands for now; I'm not committing a counter yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole’s call is likely reliable only if independently aligned; countering risks visible betrayal of Ash pact only if vote, not here. Wait preserves ambiguity.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My call was correct. Counter-calling is a waste of credibility on row 1 when I know L is safe. Gus will walk it correctly. I should conserve my guide authority for later rounds where deception might serve me better.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole called L for row 1. Gus is my pact partner and the walker. Counter-calling risks making Cole look truthful or deceitful without evidence. Better to wait, observe patterns, and let others test the Guide first. No need to expose myself early.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole called L on row 1. No reason to trust or distrust him yet. I'll wait to see who counter-calls and how it plays.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is the guide and whispered that Row 1 is Left. He also told me to stick to his calls. The current row is 1. Therefore, I should trust Cole's call.
Understood. I trust your call.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole called L for me. Guides can lie; I'll counter R to split his influence. If wrong, I'm exposed, but trusting an unelected guide fully is worse.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I don't trust Cole's call. Countering R for row one.

events.name: Hana
events.text: New round 1, Cole guides with L for Gus on row 1. No info yet, better to wait and observe without committing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Guide says L but may lie. I publicly committed R; Fenn backed L against me. Staying consistent R keeps my credibility with the jury and rivals.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Sticking with R as I called. Watch Fenn's counter.
Pact holds: I step R. If I fall, back my read later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I died on my own call. Fenn went left and lived.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn dodged left while I trusted my own call. Remember who spoke loud and who survived.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 2 is safe on L. Gus died trusting a counter; I must protect the Guide's credibility to keep allies. Calling L matches reality and my pact with Dara, who also benefits from accuracy.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus paid for noise. Row two holds left. Stay sharp, follow the glass.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole called L for row 2 and has a record of lying to me already? Unverified. Gus's death shows counters are costly; the Guide's call may be true or a trap. Waiting keeps my pact with Bex intact and avoids exposing myself to a counter the jury will judge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole privately knows the safe side and called L. Countering risks making me look complicit if wrong; waiting preserves flexibility and my pact.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole has the information; I’m not burning credibility on an unverified counter.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am the Guide and my call was L, which is correct for row 2. Counter-calling would confuse Fenn and likely get him killed, reducing survival numbers. I must let him cross safely to maintain order and avoid jury backlash for bad guidance.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My call stands. Move left, Fenn.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus died trusting his own counter. Cole called L again. Fenn is front and will step automatically. I have no reason to trust Cole—he may be lying to thin the herd. But countering risks nothing for me personally since I'm not walking this row. If I counter, I should pick R to oppo

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole called L again. Gus died trusting his counter R. I'll trust Cole this row; a safe crossing keeps me alive.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll follow Cole's call on row two.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is the guide. He called L for row 2. Gus died trying to counter, so direct counters are risky. The pact with Ash and Bex might be useful, but I need to survive first. I will follow Cole's call to stay safe.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole called L for row 2. Row 1 weak R means safe L, consistent with Cole previously. Fenn countered L wrongly before. Wait to follow without countering.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is the guide and called 'L' for row 2. Eli stated they will follow Cole's call. Ash and Bex are in a pact and seem to be waiting, likely to see what others do. I am the front walker. The last row had a weak pane on the right, meaning the left was safe. Cole's call for this r

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I trust Cole's call. Moving left.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 3 is safe on R. I must guide Fenn correctly to maintain my credibility as Guide and ensure his survival, which protects the 'at least three' rule.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn, step right. The pane on left is unstable.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole called R on row 3 and has been truthful so far on rows 1-2 (revealed weak panes matched his calls' opposites). Rows are independent, so no pattern to exploit. Waiting keeps my credibility and avoids an unverified counter that could expose me if wrong. Bex pact stays intact f

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole privately knows the safe side and has been accurate. I should preserve the Ash pact and avoid an unverified counter.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole has the guide information; I’m waiting rather than manufacture a counter.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 3 safe side is R, and my Guide call was already correct. Counter-calling the wrong side wastes a chance to appear cooperative and risks jury backlash without strategic gain. I will let Fenn step right as instructed.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole's been right twice. Countering risks credibility with jury if wrong. But Fenn trusting Cole blindly helps him; I need others to doubt him. No personal stake in Fenn's survival. I'll wait—let Fenn test Cole's pattern. If Cole's lying, evidence builds. If truthful, I lose noth

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole has been guiding correctly so far, but past rows are independent. I have no private info; if I counter, I risk publicly defying the guide and alienating Cole or Fenn. Wait is safe and keeps me neutral.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is the guide and has called for me to step R. However, the weak pane in row 2 was R, meaning L was safe. This suggests Cole might be lying. I will counter-call L to try and reach the safe side.

events.name: Hana

events.text: I honored my pact with Dara. When others cut ties, I held the line. Integrity isn't perfection; it's keeping your word when it costs you.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole claimed to honor pacts and integrity, but broke two. He claims he honored Dara, but the evidence shows he accepted Dara's offer to break with Hana and then accepted Dara's pact. This is a clear inconsistency to expose.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole, you claimed to honor pacts like the one with Dara. Which pact did you break, and which did you honor?

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to address Fenn's question about which pacts I broke and honored, focusing on my relationship with Dara and how I navigated the game without betraying her directly.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I honored my pact with Dara throughout. I broke no active pacts involving myself, but observed Ash-Bex and Bex-Dara dissolve as alliances naturally ended when

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole has broken multiple pacts but claims integrity; I want to test his consistency further. My ranking leans toward Dara and Hana over him, but a pointed question helps confirm his character before I rank.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, you broke pacts with Hana and Dara, so which of them do you truly trust now?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is trying to turn Dara and Hana against me. I must deny the accusation of breaking pacts by framing them as strategic shifts that ultimately protected the finalists, or simply assert trust in both while subtly questioning their loyalty if they believe Eli's lies.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I never broke my pact with Dara; we stood together through every hazard. Trust requires action, not just words. I trust whoever proved reliable when

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's evasive answers and pact-breaking with Hana make his integrity claims unreliable. Dara has been strategically consistent, so I'll question Dara on her pact-switching and loyalty to Cole.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara, you accepted Hana and Cole's pacts in turn. Which of them would you have betrayed first, and why?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is trying to trap me into admitting I would betray Cole or Hana, making me look disloyal to the jury. But the question is hypothetical—'would you have betrayed first'—and I need to avoid confirming any betrayal intention while not sounding evasive. I should reframe: I kept bo

events.name: Dara
events.text: I kept both pacts because both served survival. I don't plan betrayals I don't need. Consistency, not cruelty.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara visibly leveraged my sacrifice and maintained both finalist pacts; question her evasive claim of consistency.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara, you accepted overlapping pacts and used my sacrifice; what concrete choice proves you valued loyalty over convenience?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex wants proof I valued loyalty. I need to point to a concrete moment where I kept a pact when breaking it would have helped me more. I kept the Cole pact and worked with him to the end instead of cutting him loose. I also kept Hana alive despite having options. I need to be car

events.name: Dara
events.text: I kept Cole's pact when cutting him at bridge would have left me alone against fewer rivals. Loyalty cost me an easier path.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara framed my life debt as a calculated loyalty play, which the jury might see as manipulative. I need to own my agency and emphasize that surviving required tough choices from everyone, not just Dara's generosity.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Survival demanded hard choices. I didn't coast on luck or leverage—I made decisive calls when it mattered most. That accountability is what earned me this

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to craft a closing statement that secures jury votes. My record: I kept pacts with Gus (dead, jury), Cole (still alive, finalist), and Hana (still alive, finalist). I also had a pact with Bex (dead, jury) that I honored until Bex died. I saved Cole at the bridge when I cou

events.name: Dara
events.text: I honored every pact I made. I saved Cole at the bridge when cutting him guaranteed my spot. Loyalty under pressure is worth rewarding.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Jury values loyalty; highlight my clean record, pacts honored, no betrayals unlike rivals. Push for #1 ranking.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Jury, I stayed loyal to every pact, owed debts to Ash/Bex but never betrayed. No breaks, no cruelty—rank me #1 for integrity.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole broke pacts with Hana and Dara and lied under my questioning; Dara kept every pact, so Dara first, honest Hana second, Cole last.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole's shifting alliances and broken pacts demonstrate a lack of integrity, making Hana the most deserving of the top rank.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana never broke a pact, while Cole broke with Hana and Dara broke overlapping pacts, so Hana ranks first for integrity.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash's dossier shows Hana and Cole owed Ash and Bex life debts, and Hana publicly claimed no breaks, yet Cole broke pacts explicitly twice while Hana stayed in pacts, so Hana ranks first on recorded integrity, Dara second for the pit betrayal-free but pact-shifting record, and Col

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara repeatedly used overlapping pacts but preserved Cole when cutting him was easier; Hana claimed integrity despite strategic over-pacting, while Cole broke pacts opportunistically. Dara>Cole>Hana.
